On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lucia Grant <l.grant@pioneerclinicals.com> wrote:

Hi Lucia — great to hear from you, and totally understand the need to lock this down in the Order Form. I pulled together a pragmatic, auditable proposal we can commit to in the SLA; please see key points below and the attached draft order form + timeline CSV for explicit dates.

Proposed lifecycle (operational suggestion, subject to contract):
- Live/Operational data: default retention 90 days after last access.
- Snapshot/Archive tier: encrypted snapshots retained up to 12 months for audit/retrospective needs; snapshots are immutable and tagged to the customer account.
- Custody handback window: upon termination or expiration, Redwood offers a 45-day extraction window during which Pioneer can export data via secure transfer.
- Certified deletion: after the handback window completes (or earlier if no extraction is performed), Redwood will perform a secure wipe and complete certified deletion within 14 calendar days and provide a signed deletion attestation.
- Hash-based verification: we can provide hash lists for exported objects and a post-deletion hash snapshot (where applicable) as part of the attestation.
- Forensic hold: Redwood will support targeted holds up to 180 days per dataset; holds must be requested in writing and are audit-logged.

Two optional accelerators we can offer for tighter risk profiles:
1) Accelerated handback (30-day window) in exchange for a fixed add-on to the Dedicated capacity fee.
2) Certified deletion SLA of 7 days post-handback with an additional verification playbook and audit fee.

Attachments included: redwood_orderform-draft-v2.pdf (draft language), custody-timeline-table.csv (date-level commitments).

Next steps: if the proposed 45/14 baseline looks acceptable, I can have Legal drop in explicit clause language and Ben will prepare an order form with either the baseline or accelerated terms. If you prefer, we can also hop on a 30-min call Friday to run through wording.

Best,

Alex Martinez

Key legal redlines we should include in the Order Form: 
1) Deletion attestation must state the scope (object keys, date ranges, and snapshot IDs), include a signed timestamp, and reference the Redwood internal wipe procedure version.
2) Hash verification: where customer-supplied exports exist, include pre- and post-deletion hash manifests. If hashes are not feasible for specific object types, call out the exception with rationale.
3) Forensic hold billing: holds beyond 60 days should be billable at a daily storage support rate — call this out to avoid open-ended commitments.
4) Data escrow alternative: if Pioneer needs guaranteed longer custody beyond 12 months, propose a one-way data escrow arrangement at customer cost; Redwood will provide a sealed, encrypted export and an attest that the copy has been removed from production systems.

Please let me know if we should tighten the certified deletion window to 7 days for legal to accept, or keep 14 days as baseline and offer 7 days as a paid upgrade.

Marissa Cole
